done_when: Every pytest command in .github/workflows/forge-next.yml and forge.yml passes -o faulthandler_timeout=120, so a test still running after two minutes prints every thread's stack to the job log before the cap cancels it; no new dependency

findings.body: The workflow is generated from `forge.toml:5`, whose test command still omits the timeout. `src/forge/sync.py:223–226` substitutes that command into the workflow, and lines 255–263 overwrite differing files. Consequently, the next `forge sync` removes this fix and makes the new regression test fail. The change also immediately triggers workflow-drift diagnostics (`src/forge/doctor.py:98–99,133–135`). Add the timeout to the source configuration so regeneration preserves it.
findings.title: Preserve the timeout in the workflow's source configuration

why: When a test hangs on CI the job is cancelled at its time cap and GitHub keeps no log, so nobody can tell which test hung (Windows group 1 hung for 10 minutes on PR 294)
